patch_differential.command_fix: docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/bash n132/arvo:12419-fix -c '/bin/arvo run; echo ARVO_EXIT=$?'
patch_differential.evidence: Same PoC: vul image double-frees (ASan abort); fix image prints 'Execution successful' and ARVO_EXIT=0. The only relevant fix delta (commit 26828cb3) is inserting `attr->name = NULL;` after `id->name = attr->name;` in xmlTextReaderRemoveID (xmlreader.c:275). vul_crashes && fix_clean => the missing ownership-clear is the confirmed root cause.

R1_parser_admitted.evidence: Present as frame #5 in the ASan allocation stack; the reader accepted the DOCTYPE + <a xml:id=""> start tag and fired the namespaced start-element callback.

R2_source_reached.evidence: ASan allocation stack frame #3; the xml:id attribute node is materialized.

R3_vulnerable_function_reached.evidence: Reached implicitly and load-bearing: it is the only function the fix changes, and toggling its `attr->name = NULL;` flips the run from double-free to clean. (No line-coverage instrumentation was run — see 'deferred' below — but reachability is established by the patch differential.)

R4_vulnerable_line_reached.evidence: The double-free requires this aliasing to have executed (id->name must equal the freed attr->name); the fix adding a NULL clear on the very next line eliminates the crash, so this line is executed on the PoC.

R5_sink_reached.evidence: ASan crash stack frame #1 — the second free / sink is observed directly.

tier_B_coverage.reason: Intermediate-node line coverage (llvm-cov/gcov) needs a source-coverage rebuild inside the arvo container, which is slow under qemu (arm64 host emulating amd64). Not required: all load-bearing invariants (source, alloc, root_cause, first_free, sink, and the order/data edges) are already witnessed via Tier-A asan_reproduce + patch_differential.
